text: Write an event loop: a queue, registered listeners, and dispatch. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static final Deque<Object> queue = new ArrayDeque<>();
static final Map<Class<?>,List<Listener>> listeners = new LinkedHashMap<>();
static void on(Class<?> k, Listener l) { listeners.computeIfAbsent(k, x -> new ArrayList<>()).add(l); }
explanation: Verified: `got a` then `got b`. Thirty lines and it is a real event loop — take the next event, deliver it to whoever registered, repeat. Every graphical program you have used is running one. Because events are handled one at a time, handler code needs no locks, which is a large simplification and why the design has survived fifty years.
